themes.note: Two themes follow the macOS system appearance via <html data-theme>. The frontmatter carries the dark values, which are also the pre-hydration fallback. Each colorMeta entry carries its light counterpart in `lightValue`. The source ships no light surface; the light theme is derived from its documented inverse tokens because macOS system appearance is a design surface for this app.

accent.purpose: The one chromatic accent. Four jobs only: brand mark, focus ring, link emphasis, and the current-object marker (active-tab rule, selected-row edge, drop targets). Extended to the bookmark star and the sidebar resizer, which mark an object the user singled out.

accent-strong.purpose: Hover on a filled CTA, and every body-text link. #5e6ad2 lands at 4.4:1 on canvas, under the 4.5:1 text must hold; this step clears 7.2:1.

accent-focus.purpose: The focus ring and the pressed state of the primary button.

bg.purpose: The reading field, the active tab, and the iframe backdrop. Near-pure black with a faint blue tint — never #000000. Sits BELOW the chrome so an artifact reads as a lifted panel.

bg-chrome.purpose: Sidebar, toolbar, tab strip, table headers, code blocks. One step above canvas: the frame around the artifact. The source's inverse-surface-1 (#f5f6f6) sits only 2% off white, which across a full window reads as one flat field; the light value takes one extra step so the planes survive the theme switch.

bg-row-hover.purpose: Row hover across explorer, bookmarks, tabs and start page. Also inline code.

bg-elevated.purpose: Floating overlays — Quick Open, context menu, toast — plus status badges and kbd chips.

bg-row-selected.purpose: The deepest lift: a selected row or menu item. Always paired with the 2px accent marker, because one ladder step cannot carry selection alone.

border.purpose: Every boundary inside the layout: pane seams, band rules, table cells, code-block edges. This system draws structure with hairlines, not shadows.

border-strong.purpose: Floating-overlay edges, hovered button edges, the blockquote rule, a focused input.

border-tertiary.purpose: Nested surfaces, the idle bookmark star, scrollbar thumb on hover.

fg.purpose: Headings, active labels, folder names, primary chrome text.

fg-strong.purpose: Reading-field body, explorer file labels, menu items, code.

fg-muted.purpose: Secondary chrome, eyebrows, captions, hints. Clears 5.4:1 on the lightest surface in the ladder.

fg-dim.purpose: Decoration and disabled states ONLY — chevrons, idle stars, disabled buttons. At 3.1:1 it never carries text a user must read.

fg-path.purpose: Directory paths. Holds the same value as fg-muted; it stays a separate token because a path's contrast floor is a constraint worth naming and checking. Aliased to fg-muted in CSS so the two cannot drift apart in one theme only.

label-active-fg.purpose: The label of a hovered or selected row — the one step above Ink.

on-accent.purpose: Label on a lavender fill: the primary button and the brand mark.

error-fg.purpose: Failure text only: unreadable file, rejected deep link, destructive menu item, bookmark removal on hover. Not a second accent.

code-bg.purpose: Inline code spans in rendered Markdown.

code-fg.purpose: Inline code text. Ink, not a hue — syntax color belongs to Shiki inside a block. Aliased to fg-strong in CSS — the same ink step in both themes.

pre-bg.purpose: Fenced code blocks, on the chrome surface with a hairline edge.

button-hover-bg.purpose: Hover fill on icon buttons in the toolbar, tab strip and sidebar header.

badge-bg.purpose: Status badges, the zoom control, kbd chips. Pill-shaped, because pills mark status and never actions.

badge-fg.purpose: Label inside a status badge. Aliased to fg-strong in CSS — the same ink step in both themes.

empty-fg.purpose: Empty-state copy in the preview pane. Aliased to fg-muted in CSS so the two cannot drift apart in one theme only.

input-border.purpose: Resting border of the address bar.

input-border-focus.purpose: Focused border of the address bar. The field strengthens its hairline rather than taking the accent — the accent's focus job is the ring.

resizer-hover.purpose: The 6px sidebar resizer while hovered or dragging, at 60% opacity. Aliased to accent in CSS: it IS the accent, not a copy of its value.

star-active.purpose: A bookmarked file's star. Extends the current-object marker to an object the user singled out. Aliased to accent in CSS: it IS the accent, not a copy of its value.

star-idle.purpose: An unbookmarked file's star, revealed at 35% opacity until the row is hovered. Aliases border-tertiary rather than copying its value.

display-md.purpose: The start-page wordmark, SF Pro Display at 40px/600 with tracking at -0.025em. One instance in the product. There is no serif in this system.

headline.purpose: Markdown h1. Display cut at 2em/600, tracking -0.03em, over a hairline rule.

card-title.purpose: Markdown h2. Display cut at 1.5em/600, tracking -0.02em, over a hairline rule.

body.purpose: The reading field at 16px/1.5, plus the Quick Open input and the file-notice title.

body-sm.purpose: Explorer rows, start rows, menu items, bookmarks and Markdown tables at 14px.

ui.purpose: The chrome default at 13px: tabs, sidebar header, toolbar, address bar. One step below the reading field, because app chrome is denser than a page.

caption.purpose: Paths, badges, hints, footers and kbd chips at 12px.

eyebrow.purpose: Section labels at 12px/500 with POSITIVE tracking (+0.4px). Every other step tracks negative; the reversal is what marks a label as taxonomy rather than voice. It replaces uppercase micro-caps — do not reintroduce text-transform.

mono.purpose: Machine text at 13px: paths, the address bar, code blocks, plain text, kbd chips, the metadata renderer. A path is set in mono everywhere it appears.

shadows.name: menu-lift
shadows.purpose: Context menu and toast: surfaces with nothing below them to lift against. Pure black — a tinted shadow would add a hue the palette does not contain. Nothing inside the layout gets a resting shadow.

shadows.name: overlay-lift
shadows.purpose: Quick Open, over a rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6) pure-black scrim.

shadows.name: edge-highlight
shadows.purpose: The signature detail: one hairline of white light on the top edge of a lifted panel. It is what makes a dark surface read as rendered rather than as an absence. Floating overlays only.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: State feedback: hover, focus, opacity reveal, chevron rotation.

motion.name: dur
motion.purpose: Surface changes: the resizer paint, the toast rise.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single easing curve. Fast out, settled in.

motion.name: notice-rise
motion.purpose: The toast enters with a 4px rise so its arrival is legible without moving the artifact.

motion.name: start-rise
motion.purpose: The start page enters with a 6px rise — the one place the product has room for a slower beat.

motion.name: tab-pulse
motion.purpose: The loading dot on a tab whose file is still reading, pulsing 25%-100%.

layoutConstants.name: tabstrip-band
layoutConstants.purpose: The tab strip, spanning the WHOLE window above both panes. It doubles as the overlay title bar: it drags the window and reserves the traffic-light gutter.

layoutConstants.name: titlebar-gutter
layoutConstants.purpose: Reserved space for the macOS traffic lights at the head of the tab strip, before the first tab.

layoutConstants.name: header-band
layoutConstants.purpose: Sidebar header and toolbar. Equal by requirement: they sit side by side under the tab strip, so their bottom borders form one unbroken rule rather than a 1px step at the sidebar seam.

layoutConstants.name: sidebar-max
layoutConstants.purpose: Sidebar clamp ceiling. The sidebar split is the only elastic axis in the product.

layoutConstants.name: resizer-target
layoutConstants.purpose: Pointer target of the sidebar resizer, carried by a pseudo-element straddling the seam. The resizer itself takes ZERO width: as a 6px flex column it opened a transparent gap through the chrome bands that broke the rule those band heights exist to produce.

layoutConstants.name: start-measure
layoutConstants.purpose: The start-page column. The reading field imposes no measure — an artifact controls its own layout.

layoutConstants.name: overlay-width
layoutConstants.purpose: Quick Open, opened at 12vh from the top.

narrative.northStar: The chrome is a dark frame; the artifact is the protagonist.
narrative.overview: A near-black artifact reading room in the Linear idiom. A four-step surface ladder carries every hierarchy, 1px hairlines replace shadows inside the layout, and one lavender-blue accent (#5e6ad2) is spent on four jobs and no others. The reading field sits at canvas depth and the chrome lifts one step above it, so a self-contained HTML page reads as a lifted panel inside a dark frame — the same relationship Linear builds between a page and a product screenshot. Type is SF Pro at 500-600 with tracking pulled negative on display and positive on the eyebrow.
keyCharacteristics: Canvas is #010102, not #000000 — the faint blue tint is what keeps the surface from reading as a hole.
Four-step surface ladder: canvas -> chrome -> row-hover -> elevated -> row-selected. No level is skipped.
Hairlines, not shadows. Shadow survives only on the three floating overlays, and it is pure black.
One lavender accent with exactly four jobs: brand mark, focus ring, link emphasis, current-object marker.
Negative tracking on display, positive on the eyebrow. The reversal is the label signal.
The plane order is inverted from the previous system: the artifact now sits on the deepest surface.
No serif and no second display family. Weight and tracking carry the wordmark.
Two themes, because macOS system appearance is a design surface. The light theme is derived from the source's inverse tokens.
rules: Spend lavender on the four documented jobs, and count them.
Never fill an element with the accent to say 'selected' — pair a surface lift with the 2px marker.
Move one step at a time on the surface ladder.
Draw every in-layout boundary as a 1px hairline, and never let a transparent element cut one — the sidebar resizer is an overlay for exactly this reason.
Give floating overlays the edge highlight; give nothing inside the layout a resting shadow.
Ship the focus ring solid. The source specifies 50% alpha, which lands near 1.9:1 on this canvas — below the 3:1 a focus indicator must hold.
Keep fg-dim off anything a user has to read.
Set paths in mono, everywhere they appear.
A CTA is 8px. Pills mark status, never actions.
File glyphs carry shape, never hue. Two tones: subject artifacts and everything else.
The tab strip spans the whole window and reserves a 78px traffic-light gutter; the 40px header band exists so the sidebar header and toolbar rules meet across the seam.
A focusable control must be visible when it holds focus, even if it hides at rest.
dos: Keep the canvas at #010102 and let the artifact be the brightest thing on screen.
Use the four-step ladder for hierarchy instead of reaching for a shadow.
Pull tracking negative as display size grows, and positive on the eyebrow.
Pair a surface lift with the 2px accent marker to say 'current'.
Give Quick Open, the context menu and the toast the same shape: 12px, strong hairline, shadow, edge highlight.
Truncate Quick Open paths at the tail and start-page paths at the head — each keeps the segment that disambiguates.
Route failure through error-fg only, and name the problem before offering the machine reason.
Keep informational micro-text at fg-muted or above.
donts: Don't introduce a second chromatic accent. Red is failure, not color.
Don't use lavender as a section background, a row fill, or a hover state.
Don't tint a shadow, and don't put a resting shadow inside the layout.
Don't reintroduce a serif, a second display family, or uppercase micro-caps.
Don't add gradients, spotlight cards, backdrop-filter, or translucent chrome.
Don't let chrome grow with the window or add responsive breakpoints — the sidebar split is the only elastic axis.
